svg.title: Factors affecting enzyme activity
svg.desc: Graphs of enzyme activity against temperature with an optimum and denaturation, against pH for pepsin, salivary amylase and trypsin, and against substrate concentration levelling off when active sites are saturated.
svg.text: Typical human enzymes; graph shapes to learn.

g.data-info: Rate rises as molecules move faster and collide more often, up to an optimum (about 37–40 °C for human enzymes); above it, the enzyme denatures — the active site loses its shape — and the rate falls steeply.
Each enzyme has an optimum pH; either side, ionic and hydrogen bonds in the protein are disrupted and the active site changes shape. Pepsin ≈ 2, salivary amylase ≈ 7, trypsin ≈ 8.
Rate rises as more substrate means more collisions with active sites, then levels off when all the active sites are occupied (saturated).
